newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends steady to down on export skepticism.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends steady to down on export skepticism.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed unchanged to lower on skepticism that the U.S. corn export sales pace will remain active, traders said.
"The domestic market in the east (U.S. Midwest) is steady but the Gulf and West Coast markets are backing down a little," said Paul Haugens of FIMAT Futures.
Corn rose Thursday on a greater-than-expected number in USDA's weekly export sales report. But traders and analysts said such a sales pace was not likely to continue.
For instance, trading specialists said China would import 1.1 million tonnes less U.S. corn than last year.

China has harvested a record domestic crop. Also, USDA has trimmed its estimate for Mexico's demand by 2.4 million tonnes and cut exports to South Korea by two million tonnes because that country is expected to buy cheaper feedwheat.
But corn futures were underpinned by the likelihood that light or no deliveries will be posted against the December contract on first notice day Nov 29.
Corn closed unchanged to one cent lower, with December unchanged at $2.72-1/2 per bushel.
"It's very quiet and continued evening up of the December positions," Haugens said.
E.D. and F. Man International bull spread four million bushels of December/March and Merrill Lynch Futures did two million bushels of December/May, traders said.
The four and 20-day moving averages before the open Friday showed a bullish turn in the December but the March and May remained bearish.
First support in the December was $2.71 and second support was $2.68-1/4. First resistance in the December was $2.73-3/4 and second resistance was $2.76-1/2.
The daily short term nine day relative strength index (RSI) for December closed at 55.5 points The market generally considers an RSI of 70 or more as overbought and 30 or less as oversold.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 55,000 contracts, below the 68,171 traded Thursday, according to the CBOT.
In corn options, LFG Futures bought 500 March $2.90 calls and sold 500 March $3.00 calls, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 14,000 contracts, below the 14,599 traded Thursday.
